## Accessibility statement for the NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook

This statement applies to the Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. It does not cover the other
NHSBSA sites and playbooks linked from it, which publish their own statements.

We want as many people as possible to be able to use this playbook. It is built to meet the Web
Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA, and meets several level AAA criteria as
well.

## What we have done

The site is built from text, so its content is headings, paragraphs, lists, tables and links, not
pictures of them. Each diagram is described in words.

- Every page has a title, one main heading, and headings that never skip a level
- A skip link is the first thing a keyboard reaches, and takes you to the page itself. The sidebar
  and the navigation bar show which page you are on in words and in shape, not in colour alone
- Links say where they go. Source numbers link to a Sources list at the foot of the page, and
  nothing pops up over the text
- Every table has a caption and a header row. Where a first column names each row, it is marked as
  row headers, so a screen reader can say which row a cell is in
- Text reflows to one column at 320 pixels wide, and at 400 percent zoom, without sideways
  scrolling. On a phone or a short window the bars stay in the page and are not pinned over it
- On a phone the sidebar takes focus when it opens, gives it back when it closes, and puts the page
  behind it out of reach
- Every control that takes keyboard focus shows a ring of two colours, so that it can be seen on a
  light or a dark ground
- Each diagram has a text description under it, and opens on its own page as an SVG that scales to
  any zoom. On a narrow screen it scrolls sideways inside its own box, which WCAG 1.4.10 allows for
  content that needs two dimensions to mean anything. Its labels sit beside the shapes they name, so
  they are part of a picture and not an image of text
- Animation is switched off for anyone who has asked their device for less motion
- Text and interface colours meet the required contrast, and nothing relies on colour alone

The playbook can also be built as a tagged PDF, an editable Word file and a tour of the site in
photographs. These are alternative views of the web version, made on request, and they are not the
published playbook. Each has a language, a title, an outline or heading styles, alternative text for
every picture, and captions and header rows on every table.

## What we have checked, and how

These claims are checked against the built pages every time the site is rebuilt, rather than being
asserted once. An accessibility engine tests every page against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 at levels A
and AA, on a laptop window, a phone window and a phone window at 400 percent zoom. Our own checks
then test what an engine cannot see: that every table has a caption and row headers, that the skip
link lands at the top of the page, that the current page is the one marked as current, that Tab
never leaves a control off screen or under a fixed bar, and that no line of text runs past 80
characters, counted rather than estimated. Two checks work from a photograph of the screen: every
kind of control is given keyboard focus and photographed either side, and the words printed on a
control are compared with the name it speaks.

## Where we go beyond level AA

Five level AAA criteria are met and checked the same way.

| Criterion | What it asks | What the site does |
|---|---|---|
| 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced) | 7:1 for body text, 4.5:1 for large text | Links are NHS Dark Blue at 11.85:1, quiet text is NHS Dark Grey at 7.75:1, and white on the title banner clears 7:1 |
| 1.4.8 Visual Presentation | No line longer than 80 characters, no justified text, generous spacing | No line of text is longer than 80 characters on any page at two window widths, set ragged right, with line spacing of 1.5 or more |
| 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) | Anything you click or tap is at least 44 by 44 pixels | Navigation, footer, contents and card links, and the menu and sidebar buttons, are 44 pixels each way. A link in a sentence takes the exception for inline targets |
| 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only) | Every link makes sense on its own | No link reads "click here" or "read more", or uses a web address as its text. Every link is checked on every build |
| 2.4.10 Section Headings | Content is organised under headings | Every page of any length carries headings, so the on-this-page list is a usable route |

: The level AAA criteria the site meets, what each asks and what the site does

## Where we do not meet level AAA

We do not claim level AAA for the whole site. The W3C advises against requiring it as a general
policy, because some content cannot meet every AAA criterion. Two are out of reach for guidance of
this kind.

**3.1.4 Expansion of short forms** asks that the meaning of every short form is available. Most are
spelled out where they first appear, and a few, such as ARIMA, are not.

**3.1.5 Reading Level** asks for text a person with lower secondary education can understand, or a
simpler version. The Resource pages cite clause numbers from GovS 010 and the AQuA Book and use the
vocabulary of analytical assurance, because their readers need the exact terms. The glossary in
Resources is a partial answer.

## What we have not tested

No screen reader, magnifier or speech input testing has been carried out against the published
site, and none on a real phone or tablet. What has been tested is the markup and what a browser
shows, by an accessibility engine, by our own measurements and by walking the keyboard through the
site at several screen sizes. Automated checks find only the faults they are written to look for.

Some corrections, including the skip link and the names of the navigation landmarks, are made by a
script when the page loads. With scripts switched off the pages still read in order, but those
corrections are missing.

Parts of this site may still not be fully accessible, and this statement describes the work done
rather than a tested result. If you find a problem, we want to hear about it.

## Reporting a problem

If you find a problem that is not listed here, or you need content in a different format, write to
[analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk](mailto:analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk). Tell us the page,
what you were trying to do, and what happened.

## Enforcement procedure

The Equality and Human Rights Commission is responsible for enforcing the Public Sector Bodies
(Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018. If you are not happy with
how we respond to your complaint, contact the
[Equality Advisory and Support Service](https://www.equalityadvisoryservice.com/).
